title: Panasonic TV will not power on
fullDescription:
Panasonic legacy plasma TVs (TC-P/TX-P series) commonly fail to start due to PSU capacitor failures - the so-called '10 blink' code or no LED.

Newer OLED models (HZ/JZ/LZ series) are more reliable but PSU caps still degrade over 8+ years.

fixSteps.title: Capacitor inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Open back, look for bulged caps.

affectedModels: TC-P plasma, Viera LCD, HZ/JZ/LZ OLED
whenToCallPro: PSU work needs experience - plasma especially has high voltages.
videoSearchQuery: Panasonic TV won't turn on fix

faq.a: Some - check eBay and specialist suppliers; common parts still findable.

title: Panasonic blinking LED diagnostic codes
shortDescription: Standby LED blinks indicate fault category.
fullDescription:
Panasonic plasma and Viera LCD TVs use blink codes for diagnostics:
- 7 blinks: SC board (plasma)
- 10 blinks: SS or SU board
- 14 blinks: Main board

Count blinks across multiple cycles to identify the failed board.

fixSteps.title: Count blinks
fixSteps.instruction: Count repeating pattern - decode using Panasonic service manual.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 5 minutes; sometimes clears soft faults.

fixSteps.title: Replace identified board
fixSteps.instruction: Order matching board by part number.

whenToCallPro: Plasma board work involves high voltages - call pro.

faq.q: Is the blink code in the manual?
faq.a: Yes - service manuals list code-to-board mapping.

displayCode: Firefox OS / My Home Screen Stuck
title: My Home Screen interface frozen
fullDescription:
Panasonic uses Firefox OS / My Home Screen on smart TVs. It can freeze due to cache or app issues. Power cycle resolves most cases.

Newer 2023+ models use Google TV instead.
affectedModels: Panasonic My Home Screen / Firefox OS / Google TV

faq.a: Updates ended; newer Panasonic uses Google TV.

title: HDMI input shows no signal
fullDescription: Panasonic 'No Signal' issues are usually wrong input or cable problems. Higher-end OLEDs (LZ2000, MZ2000) need HDMI Mode set to High Speed for 4K/120.

fixSteps.title: HDMI Mode High
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Setup > HDMI Auto Setting > Mode 2.

faq.a: Panasonic's High Speed mode for HDMI 2.0/2.1 features.

title: Panasonic TV no audio
fullDescription: Panasonic audio issues come from output settings or Atmos passthrough mismatch. Higher-end OLED+ models with Technics-tuned speakers can have specific driver failures.

faq.a: Panasonic's audio brand tunes premium OLED speakers.

title: Viera Link HDMI-CEC not working
fullDescription: Viera Link is Panasonic's HDMI-CEC. Failures usually mean it's been disabled, partner CEC is off, or cable doesn't carry CEC.

fixSteps.title: Enable Viera Link
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Setup > Viera Link Settings > Viera Link ON.

title: Audible buzzing from plasma TV
shortDescription: Plasma display panel buzzing or humming.
fullDescription:
Panasonic plasma TVs commonly emit a buzzing sound that varies with image content. This is normal panel operation but excessive buzz indicates failing capacitors on the SC/SS boards.

High-altitude operation (above 6500 ft) increases buzz - Panasonic explicitly mentions this.

fixSteps.title: Reduce contrast
fixSteps.instruction: Lower Contrast and Brightness to reduce buzz.

fixSteps.title: Cell light setting
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Picture > Cell Light - lower value.

fixSteps.title: Service caps
fixSteps.instruction: If excessive, SC/SS board capacitor refresh.

whenToCallPro: If excessive buzz with brightness reduced.

faq.a: Yes - all plasmas buzz slightly; it's not a defect.

title: Firmware update did not install
fullDescription: Panasonic update failures usually trace to network instability. Panasonic supports USB updates - download firmware from local Panasonic support site (different per region).

fixSteps.title: USB update
fixSteps.instruction: Download regional firmware, copy to USB root.

faq.a: Panasonic regional support sites - region-specific firmware.

title: Vertical lines on display
fullDescription: Vertical lines on Panasonic LCDs and OLEDs indicate T-CON or panel failure. Plasma TVs more commonly show patches or full sections going dark instead of lines.

fixSteps.title: Confirm internal
fixSteps.instruction: Lines on menu confirm internal fault.

faq.a: Rarely - plasma failures show as section blackouts or buzzing instead.

title: Panasonic remote unresponsive
fullDescription: Panasonic uses IR remotes; touchpad remotes on premium models use Bluetooth. The N2QAYB and similar IR remotes are reliable - failure is usually batteries or sensor blockage.

fixSteps.title: IR test
fixSteps.instruction: Use phone camera to confirm IR LED flashes.

fixSteps.title: Re-pair touchpad
fixSteps.instruction: Premium models - hold OK + Return 5 seconds.

faq.a: Yes - Panasonic codes are widely supported.
